healthy.fix: Your plant looks good! Keep watering consistently at the soil line, give it 6-8 hours of sun, and check leaves weekly for early signs of trouble.

early_blight.cause: A fungus that thrives in warm, humid conditions and splashes up from the soil onto lower leaves.
early_blight.fix: Remove and discard affected leaves (don't compost them). Mulch around the base to stop soil splashing onto leaves. Spray a mix of 1 tbsp baking soda + 1 tsp liquid soap + 1 gallon water once a week.

late_blight.cause: A fast-spreading water mold favored by cool, wet weather - the same disease behind the Irish potato famine.
late_blight.fix: Remove and destroy infected leaves/plants immediately, this one spreads fast. Water at the soil, not the leaves, and space plants for airflow. A copper fungicide spray (garden-center staple) helps protect healthy growth.

bacterial_spot.cause: Bacteria that spread through wet leaves, splashing water, and contaminated tools.
bacterial_spot.fix: Remove affected leaves, avoid overhead watering, and disinfect pruning tools with rubbing alcohol between cuts. A weekly copper-based spray helps slow the spread.

septoria_leaf_spot.cause: A fungus that starts on lower, older leaves in warm, wet weather.
septoria_leaf_spot.fix: Prune off spotted lower leaves and improve airflow between plants. Mulch to stop soil splash. Weekly baking soda spray (1 tbsp baking soda + 1 tsp liquid soap + 1 gallon water) helps control mild cases.

leaf_mold.cause: A fungus that loves high humidity and poor air circulation, common in greenhouses or crowded plantings.
leaf_mold.fix: Space plants out and prune to increase airflow, water at the soil only, and remove moldy leaves. Spray with a baking-soda solution (1 tbsp baking soda + 1 tsp liquid soap + 1 gallon water) every few days until it clears.

spider_mites.cause: Tiny pests that thrive in hot, dry conditions and suck fluid from leaves, leaving stippled/yellow spots and fine webbing.
spider_mites.fix: Spray leaves (top and underside) forcefully with water every couple of days to knock mites off. Follow with a mix of 1 tsp mild dish soap + 1 quart water as a spray. Keep the plant well-watered, mites prefer stressed, dry plants.

target_spot.cause: A fungus that produces distinctive bullseye-ringed spots, favored by warm, humid, wet-leaf conditions.
target_spot.fix: Remove affected leaves and avoid wetting foliage when watering. Improve spacing/airflow. A weekly copper fungicide or baking-soda spray (1 tbsp baking soda + 1 tsp liquid soap + 1 gallon water) helps manage it.

mosaic_virus.cause: A virus spread by handling plants (including smoking/tobacco residue on hands) and by insects like aphids. Not curable.
mosaic_virus.fix: There's no cure, remove and discard (don't compost) infected plants to protect the rest. Wash hands and tools with soap after handling, and control aphids going forward.

yellow_leaf_curl_virus.cause: A virus spread by whiteflies, causing yellowing, upward-curling leaves and stunted growth. Not curable.
yellow_leaf_curl_virus.fix: Remove and discard infected plants to stop spread. Control whiteflies with a soapy water spray (1 tsp mild dish soap + 1 quart water) on leaf undersides, and use yellow sticky traps nearby.

unknown.cause: This doesn't clearly match a condition the model knows about.
unknown.fix: Try a clearer, well-lit close-up photo of the affected leaf. If symptoms persist, check with a local nursery or agricultural extension office.
